name: Bluebird Longmont (opened as Zinnia)
headline: Element Properties' Bluebird Longmont, a 55-unit permanent supportive housing building for people leaving homelessness at 2000 Sunset Way in Longmont, all at 30% AMI, won $653,854 a year in 2022 federal 9% credits and opened in October 2024 under the name Zinnia.
why_it_matters: It shows a city-plus-housing-authority land contribution, fee waivers and a housing authority tax exemption carrying a small-credit (about $11,900 per unit per year) PSH deal from award to opening in about 29 months, next to an existing housing authority PSH property for shared management.

status.label: Built and open (October 2024)
status.detail: A City of Longmont and Longmont Housing Authority development summary presented to Boulder County in February 2025 lists Zinnia at 2000 Sunset Way as completed, opened in October 2024, with 55 one-bedroom units at 30% AMI, LIHTC and state vouchers. Linking the name Zinnia to the CHFA ledger name Bluebird Longmont is inferred from the same developer, address and unit count. No 8609 or placed-in-service record was found.

next_step: Look for the property on CHFA's placed-in-service lists or HUD's LIHTC database under the name Zinnia to confirm the 8609 year and final credit amount.

key_numbers.value: 55 homes, all one-bedroom, all at 30% AMI
key_numbers.meaning: Permanent supportive housing for adults leaving homelessness, with project-based vouchers from the Colorado Division of Housing and Longmont Housing Authority.
About $6.5M over 10 years (inferred); the developer told the press the credits would raise almost $5.7M in equity.
State gap funding at $75,000 per unit, awarded in 2023 per a 2024 grant announcement.
About 29 months after the May 2022 award (inferred from the dates).

background.text: Land: the City of Longmont and the Longmont Housing Authority jointly own the parcel and agreed in 2019 to transfer it to Element under an option that was due to expire in December 2022; the narrative calls it a land contribution.
The application was a second try: the narrative says the 9% request fell almost 34% from the prior year's application after adding $2.4M of debt and seeking the maximum DOH gap funding.
Estimated total cost at application was about $331,000 per unit, of which $224,000 was hard cost (about $18.2M total for 55 units, inferred).
Local approvals: the narrative says site plan and building permit needed no discretionary approvals once an emergency access easement was secured from the neighboring mall owner.
Property tax exemption through the Longmont Housing Authority was part of the plan at application.
A 2024 grant announcement also lists CHFA private activity bonds among the funders; no bond amount or issuer record was found, and the CHFA 4% award report has no row for this deal.
Under construction in May 2024 with a target completion in October 2024.

timeline.event: Element, the City of Longmont and Longmont Housing Authority sign an option agreement for the site
Listed on CHFA's 2022 Round One applicant report ($603,092 requested)
Awarded $653,854 a year in federal 9% credits
Developer tells press it plans to break ground in spring 2023 and finish in summer 2024
Reported under construction as Zinnia, target completion October 2024

discrepancies.text: The 2022 applicant report shows $603,092 of credit requested, the narrative cites a request of $650,824, and the award report shows $653,854 awarded.
CHFA and the city's 2025 development summary give the address as 2000 Sunset Way, while the city's affordable housing resource list gives Zinnia's address as 2005 Sunset Way.
At application the lead service provider was the Boulder Shelter for the Homeless, while the 2025 city summary lists supportive services by All Roads.
